newsitem.title: UK: British Inflation hits two-year high in July.
newsitem.headline: British Inflation hits two-year high in July.

text.p: British inflation leaped to a near two-year high of 3.3 percent in July from 2.9 percent in June, official figures showed Tuesday.
The Office for National Statistics said the underlying rate of inflation, which excludes mortgage payments, jumped as well. It reached 3.0 percent in July from 2.7 percent in June.
But financial markets were unfazed. The FTSE-100 index of leading shares spurted 20 points higher to 5,052 and the pound was little changed.

Economists said the leap in July inflation was largely due to one-time effects, particularly a jump in gasoline prices following tax increases in Chancellor of the Exchequer Gordon Brown's first budget, and increased housing costs following a succession of recent interest rate rises.

"One factor that may prevent the market selling off too badly on this is that RPIY fell on the month," said Tom Rayner, economist at Societe Generale. The RPIY measure strips out mortgage interest payments and indirect taxes from the inflation equation, thus excluding any measures introduced in the July 2 budget.
That measure fell 0.2 percent between June and July and was just 2.2 percent higher than a year ago.

Inflation fears were also calmed by other components in the breakdown of Tuesday's figures. Household goods prices dropped 1.5 percent over the month while clothing and footwear prices tumbled 4.7 percent.
The Bank of England raised base interest rates for the fourth time in as many months last week, taking them to 7 percent.
